Awesome breakfast
Sep 2019 • Couples
I was staying in an apartment block in district 4 with my Vietnamese girlfriend. Our building, as I am sure are many others, has a high density of investment properties. Local Vietnamese buy them and then advertise them on air b and b. I know this because there is different set of international strangers going up and down in the lift each time. They're mostly just popping down to the small 7-11 by the entrance for their croissant or a piece of cake. 

It's a shame really because a two minute slow walk around the corner is Thanh Tuyền, which is full of locals enjoying a vastly superior meal to anything offered by 7-11. For the same price as a small piece of cake they are filling up on possibly the most delicious breakfast for some miles. 

Thanh Tuyền only do breakfast and is only open from 6 until 11. Their repertoire is reassuringly limited as with all the best street food they do one thing and do it well. Very well.

Take a seat next to a friendly local, place your order and within minutes you are delivered a sizzling cast iron platter of ground beef, pate and a fried egg with a side of fresh baguette and some salad. This is a make it yourself bánh mì. My girlfriend opted for the tear off a piece of bread and add a small amount of meat / pate / egg and repeat. All very delicate, I opted for the tear it right open and stuff everything in. Either way it's absolutely delicious. 

A previous reviewer mentioned that the portions were small. I disagree one was more than enough but if you have an appetite, order 2 and you'll still get out for well under $5.

Best breakfast in Saigon!
Jul 2019 • Solo
The map pinpoint here is quite a long way off: Truong To is actually the lane that comes south into District 4 from the footbridge at the bottom of Pasteur Street; and this restaurant is just to the right at the first intersection, a short block in from the river. Also, I think the name is actually 'Tuyen Thanh' - not that it makes any difference.

There are quite a few 'Bo Ne' places around Saigon, but this is the best I've found; it's friendly, lively, and super-cheap. (Well, I think it's now 45 or 49 for the standard plate, but that's pretty standard for good 'street food' these days, and it's a good-sized serving.)

A handful of shredded beef is flash-cooked for a few seconds in a shallow layer of oil in a sizzling dish; then they crack an egg alongside the beef and bring it to your table immediately. It literally takes about 30 seconds or so from placing your order to tucking into your meal. The egg yolk is still runny - if you dig in quickly. (The platter is ridiculously hot, so everything keeps cooking for several minutes on the table.) And you get a big splodge of very tasty pate served on top of everything, just for good measure. SO DELICIOUS!

It's served with a small banh mi baguette and a generous side salad (interestingly, here it's a 'Western' salad of onions, lettuce and tomato - which I don't think is typical for these places; but it works very well for me). You also get little dishes of dark soy sauce and mixed salt and pepper for you to add extra seasoning, if you wish. And there are the usual table condiments of sweet chilli sauce, chilli paste, etc. However, I think the beef is pre-marinated in soy (or Maggi sauce maybe - terribly popular in this country!); it's suspiciously mouth-watering already, and I don't think you really need to add anything more to it.

This is a basic, open-to-the-sidewalk restaurant, but quite a big one. And it seems to have pretty much an entirely local clientele. You have to be willing to share a table with a bunch of strangers - or perhaps even to have to wait to be seated for a while at peak periods. Staff are friendly, and a few of them speak some English.

They have very good coffee too!

I think they serve all day, but mornings seem to be especially popular. This makes a great 'steak-and-eggs' type of breakfast at the weekend - for a couple of dollars.

Bo Ne restuarant
Dec 2018 • Family
As far as I know this only serves a bo ne menu, which is beef, pate, eggs, onions, bread and tomatoes. I really enjoy this breakfast on occasions, this isn't a huge breakfast and there are other places that serve this in the mornings, but this place is my favorite. If you go on a Sunday morning you'll probably have to wait for a place to open up in the restaurant, there are many people waiting to get in. Unlike other places like this I haven't seen many tourists, if any at this place. My family and I come to this restaurant every couple of weeks, it's a little drive for us, but the food is worth it to me.
